procedural_history.impugned_order: Judgment and Order dated 08.03.2022 of the Division Bench of the High Court of Punjab & Haryana at Chandigarh in LPA No.737 of 2021.
procedural_history.high_court_proceedings: The Division Bench of the High Court of Punjab and Haryana issued an order on 08.03.2022 in LPA No.737 of 2021, which was challenged in the Supreme Court. The Supreme Court set aside the Division Bench's order and affirmed the order of the Single Judge dated 23.04.2021.
procedural_history.supreme_court_posture: The Appellants (represented by Ms. Aishwarya Bhati, A.S.G., et al.) appealed to the Supreme Court against the High Court's Division Bench order. The Supreme Court allowed the appeal, set aside the Division Bench's order, and affirmed the order of the Single Judge dated 23.04.2021, subject to observations made in the Supreme Court's judgment.

directions: The impugned order of the Division Bench of the High Court of Punjab and Haryana is set aside.
The order of the Ld. Single Judge dated 23.04.2021 is affirmed subject to observations made hereinabove.

issue.issue_text: Determination of the cut-off date qua the eligibility condition of pending disciplinary proceedings

facts: The case involved interpreting Rule 9 of the Haryana Civil Service (Executive Branch) Rules, 2008, to determine the correct cut-off date for eligibility concerning pending disciplinary proceedings.

Two potential dates were considered: 01.11.2018, which was specified in the rules for age-related eligibility, and the "date of consideration," which was the date the selection committee recommended names (31.08.2019 in this case).
As of 01.11.2018, no disciplinary action was pending or contemplated against the respondent.
However, by the date of consideration (31.08.2019), a decision had been taken to charge-sheet the respondent.
The High Court's Single Judge and Division Bench had reached opposite conclusions on which date should apply.
law: The Supreme Court analyzed Rule 9 and found that it does not contemplate a single, uniform cut-off date for all eligibility conditions.
The Court noted that only the sub-clause related to age eligibility (Rule 9(1)(a)(ii)) explicitly mentioned the date of 01.11.2018.
The sub-clause regarding disciplinary proceedings (Rule 9(1)(a)(iii)) did not specify any date.

The Court reasoned that treating 01.11.2018 as a uniform cut-off would create an anomaly, as a candidate could become subject to disciplinary action after that date but before the selection and still be considered eligible, which could not have been the rule-maker's intent.
application: The Court rejected the High Court Division Bench's finding that 01.11.2018 was the cut-off for all eligibility criteria, calling that interpretation "perverse and without any basis."
It held that the date 01.11.2018 was relevant only for determining the age of the candidate.
For the specific issue of pending or contemplated disciplinary action, the Court determined that the relevant date is the "date of consideration."
In this case, the "date of consideration" was established as 31.08.2019, the day the Committee recommended names to the Commission.
reasoning.conclusion: The Supreme Court decided that the cut-off date for determining eligibility regarding pending or contemplated disciplinary proceedings is the "date of consideration" (31.08.2019), not the fixed date of 01.11.2018, which applied only to age-related eligibility.

cases.case_name: Champaklal Chimanlal Shah vs The Union of India
cases.principle: When an order terminating services makes no imputation whatsoever against the employee, it cannot be said that the termination is visited with any evil consequences, and therefore it does not amount to the infliction of the penalty of dismissal or removal, and does not attract the protection of Article 311(2).

cases.case_name: S. Govinda Menon v. Union of India
cases.principle: The fact that other service rules may allow for suspension when 'disciplinary proceedings were contemplated' should not lead to the conclusion that a member of an All-India Service should be treated differently.

ratio_decidendi.ratio: The phrase "inquiry is contemplated" means a decision has been taken to initiate an inquiry based on material collected during a preliminary investigation which establishes a prima facie case. The term signifies a probable intention, which is a step beyond mere possibility but falls short of certainty.
obiter: The court noted that it was not strictly necessary to decide on the meaning of "contemplate" as the case could be resolved by identifying the relevant cut-off date.

judicial_reasoning.core_finding: The court concluded that for a disciplinary inquiry to be considered "contemplated" in a way that would disqualify an employee from promotion, it must be more than a mere possibility or the existence of a preliminary complaint. The appointing authority must have applied its mind to the allegations, conducted a preliminary inquiry, and reached a state of prima facie satisfaction that the allegations have substance and warrant a formal inquiry. This stage of having a "probable intention" to proceed is the crucial threshold that must be met.
legal_tests_applied: The court interpreted the word ‘contemplate’ within the service rule to mean ‘to have in view as a probable intention,’ establishing a standard that is a step ahead of mere possibility but falls short of certainty.

For an inquiry to be deemed "contemplated," the appointing authority must first be satisfied that the allegations against the government servant have substance enabling a formal disciplinary inquiry for a major penalty. This satisfaction must be reached before adverse action can be taken on the basis of a contemplated inquiry.
policy_considerations: Denying an employee promotion merely on the basis that a charge-sheet is contemplated or an investigation is ordered is "per se improper and opposed to principles of natural justice," as it interferes with a right to which the employee was rightfully entitled.
The court endorsed the principle of natural justice that "No man can be denied his due without even letting him have an inkling as to why he is being denied it.”
